practical training undertaken as part of an educational or vocational course; or
work carried out as a minister of religion or in any other capacity for the purposes of a religious organisation.

nodes.heading: Exclusion conditions where registrable offender is a child

nodes.text: In deciding whether to include a condition referred to in section 66Q(2)(c) in a prohibition order against a registrable offender who is a child, the Children's Court must consider the following—
the desirability of the child being supported to gain access to appropriate educational services and health services;
the desirability of allowing the education, training or employment of the child to continue without interruption;
the desirability of minimising disruption to the child and the importance of maintaining social networks and support which may be lost if the child were required to leave the residence.

The Children's Court may only include an exclusion condition in a prohibition order against a registrable offender who is a child if it is satisfied that, if the child is excluded from the child's residence, the child will have appropriate alternative accommodation and appropriate care and supervision.

For the purposes of considering a matter referred to in subsection (2), the Children's Court may request the Secretary to the Department of Justice and Community Safety to give the Court a report about the options available for the appropriate accommodation, care and supervision of the child if the exclusion condition were included in the prohibition order.
If the Secretary receives a request under subsection (3)—
the Secretary must give the report to the court in the period ordered by the court or, if no period is ordered, within the prescribed time; and

for a request relating to a child under the age of 17 years, section 30 of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 applies in relation to the request for the report as if the request were a report received under section 28 of that Act.

nodes.heading: Drug testing conditions and alcohol testing conditions

nodes.text: If the court includes in a prohibition order a condition referred to in section 66Q(2)(g) or (h), the court may also include a condition that the registrable offender submit to breath testing, urinalysis or other approved test procedures—
in the case of a condition referred to in section 66Q(2)(g), for the detection of alcohol; or
in the case of a condition referred to in section 66Q(2)(h), for the detection of drugs of dependence.
The Chief Commissioner of Police may approve, in writing, test procedures (other than blood tests) for the detection of alcohol or drugs of dependence for the purposes of subsection (1).

nodes.heading: Registrable offender to submit to testing for drugs and alcohol

nodes.text: If a prohibition order includes a drug testing condition or an alcohol testing condition, a police officer may direct the registrable offender, in accordance with this section, to submit to breath testing, urinalysis or other approved test procedures.

The police officer must not give a direction under subsection (1) unless the police officer has reasonable grounds to suspect that the registrable offender has contravened a condition of the prohibition order by consuming alcohol or using or unlawfully obtaining drugs of dependence (as the case requires).
Before giving the registrable offender a direction under subsection (1), the police officer must—
specify the grounds on which the police officer reasonably suspects that the registrable offender has contravened a condition of the prohibition order; and
state that the registrable offender may contravene the prohibition order by refusing to comply with the direction.
A registrable offender who is directed to submit to drug testing or alcohol testing may request that the police officer state, orally or in writing, the officer's name, rank and place of duty.
A police officer must not, in response to a request under subsection (4)—
refuse or fail to comply with the request; or
state a name or rank that is false in a material particular; or
state as the police officer's place of duty an address other than the name of the police station which is the police officer's ordinary place of duty.

nodes.heading: Monitoring conditions and powers of entry, search and seizure under monitoring conditions
Court may include monitoring conditions in a prohibition order

nodes.text: If the court considers that it is necessary to monitor the registrable offender's compliance with one or more specified conditions included in a prohibition order under section 66Q, the court may include a monitoring condition in the prohibition order.

A monitoring condition authorises a police officer, in accordance with this Division, to do any of the following for the purposes of monitoring the registrable offender's compliance with any specified conditions—
enter premises at which the registrable offender usually resides, at any time at which the police officer reasonably suspects that the registrable offender is present at those premises; and
in the presence of the registrable offender—
search and examine the premises, and any thing (including a vehicle) belonging to, or in the possession or under the control of, the registrable offender; and
seize any thing belonging to, or in the possession or under the control of, the registrable offender; and
search and examine the registrable offender at those premises.

For the purposes of a monitoring condition, the court may include a further condition requiring that the registrable offender be at premises at which the registrable offender usually resides on specified days or at specified times of day.

nodes.heading: Powers of entry under monitoring condition

nodes.text: If a prohibition order includes a monitoring condition, a police officer, at any time, may enter premises at which the registrable offender usually resides if the police officer reasonably suspects that the registrable offender is present at those premises.
If necessary, a police officer may use reasonable force to enter premises under subsection (1).
A police officer exercising a power of entry under this section—
must announce that the police officer is authorised to enter the premises by a monitoring condition included in a prohibition order; and
if the police officer has been unable to obtain unforced entry, must give any person at the premises an opportunity to allow entry to the premises.
As soon as possible after gaining entry to the premises, the police officer must inform the registrable offender that the police officer may—
search and examine the premises, and any thing (including a vehicle) belonging to, or in the possession or under the control of, the registrable offender; and
seize any thing at the premises belonging to, or in the possession or under the control of, the registrable offender; and
search and examine the registrable offender; and
detain the registrable offender for so long as is reasonably necessary to conduct a search of the registrable offender or examine any thing under section 66W;
if necessary, use such force as is reasonably necessary to conduct a search or seize any thing.
The registrable offender may request that the police officer state, orally or in writing, the officer's name, rank and place of duty.
A police officer must not, in response to a request under subsection (5)—
refuse or fail to comply with the request; or
state a name or rank that is false in a material particular; or
state as the police officer's place of duty an address other than the name of the police station which is the police officer's ordinary place of duty.
A police officer may exercise a power under this section only if the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds that the search is necessary—
to monitor the registrable offender's compliance with a condition to which the monitoring condition relates; or

because the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds the registrable offender of behaviour or conduct associated with an increased risk of contravening a condition to which the monitoring condition relates.
A police officer exercising a power of entry under a monitoring condition may search and examine—
any part of the premises occupied by the registrable offender; and
any thing (including a vehicle) belonging to, or in the possession or control of, the registrable offender; and
the registrable offender.
For the purposes of subsection (2)(c), a search of the registrable offender means either or both a garment search or a pat-down search.
To the extent practicable, a pat-down search must be conducted by a police officer of the same sex as the registrable offender being searched.

A police officer may use such force as is reasonably necessary to conduct a search or examine any thing under this section, if that use of force is authorised by the most senior police officer present during the search.
A police officer may detain the registrable offender for so long as is reasonably necessary to conduct a search or examine any thing under this section.
A search under this section may continue only for as long as necessary to achieve the purpose of the search.
In this section—

nodes.heading: garment search
nodes.text: means a search of any article of clothing worn by a person or in the person's possession, where the article of clothing is touched and removed from the person's body;

nodes.heading: pat-down search
nodes.text: means a search of a person where the person's clothed body is touched.

nodes.heading: Police officer may direct registrable offender to provide assistance—computers and other devices

nodes.text: This section applies in relation to a computer or device that belongs to, or is in the possession or under the control of, the registrable offender—
at the premises being searched under section 66W; or
that has been seized under section 66Y.
A police officer may direct the registrable offender to provide information or other assistance that is reasonably necessary to enable the police officer to—
access data held in, or accessible from, the computer or device; or
copy to a data storage device data held in, or accessible from, the computer or device; or
convert into documentary or another intelligible form—
data held in, or accessible from, the computer or device; or
data held in a data storage device to which the data was copied as described in paragraph (b).
Before giving a direction under subsection (2), the police officer must state that the registrable offender may commit an offence if the registrable offender—
has relevant knowledge of—
the computer or device or a computer network of which the computer or device forms or formed a part; or
measures applied to protect data held in, or accessible from, the computer or device; and
without reasonable excuse, fails to comply with the direction.

A registrable offender who has relevant knowledge and who has been given a warning under subsection (3) must not, without reasonable excuse, fail to comply with a direction given under subsection (2).
Penalty: Level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).
In this section—

nodes.heading: access
nodes.text: , in relation to data held in a computer or device, means—
the display of the data by the computer or device or any other output of the data from the computer or device; or
the copying or moving of the data to any other place in the computer or to a device; or
in the case of a program, the execution of the program;

nodes.heading: data
nodes.text: includes—
information in any form; and
any program or part of a program;

nodes.heading: data held in a computer or device
nodes.text: includes—

path.definition: data held in a computer or device

nodes.text: data entered or copied into the computer or device; and

path.definition: data held in a computer or device

nodes.text: data held in any removable data storage device for the time being in the computer; and

path.definition: data held in a computer or device

nodes.text: data held in a data storage device on a computer network of which the computer or device forms part;

path.definition: data held in a computer or device

nodes.heading: data storage device
nodes.text: means any thing containing or designed to contain data for use by a computer;
A USB storage device or a file server.

nodes.heading: device
nodes.text: includes a data storage device and a smartphone;

nodes.heading: relevant knowledge
nodes.text: means information or other assistance that would enable the police officer to—
access data held in, or accessible from, a computer or device that belongs to or is in the possession or under the control of the registrable offender at the premises being searched; or
copy to a data storage device data held in, or accessible from, a computer or device referred to in paragraph (a); or
convert into documentary or another intelligible form—
data held in, or accessible from, a computer or device referred to in paragraph (a); or
data held in a data storage device to which the data was copied as described in paragraph (b).

nodes.heading: Power to seize
nodes.text: In conducting a search of premises or the registrable offender under section 66W, a police officer may seize or take a sample of any thing belonging to or found in the possession or under the control of the registrable offender—
which the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds—
will compromise the registrable offender's compliance with a condition of the prohibition order to which the monitoring condition relates; or
relates to behaviour or conduct associated with an increased risk of the registrable offender contravening a condition to which the monitoring condition relates; or
if the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds that—
the thing will afford evidence of the contravention by the registrable offender of a condition to which the monitoring condition relates; and
it is necessary to seize or take a sample of that thing in order to prevent its concealment, loss or destruction.

nodes.heading: Recording and register of seized things

nodes.text: All things seized under section 66Y by a police officer must be photographed or otherwise recorded.
The Chief Commissioner of Police must establish and maintain a register of things seized under section 66Y.
The register must contain the prescribed details for each thing seized.

nodes.heading: Police officer must provide receipt for seized things

nodes.text: As soon as practicable after seizing a thing under section 66Y, a police officer must—
give the registrable offender a receipt for the thing; or
if the registrable offender refuses to accept the receipt, leave the receipt in a conspicuous place at the premises being searched.
A receipt must—
contain the prescribed information; and
be signed in accordance with the regulations.

nodes.heading: Retention of seized things by Chief Commissioner of Police
nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police may retain any thing seized under section 66Y for as long as—
one of the following conditions are met—

if the thing was seized under section 66Y(a)(i), the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds that the thing will compromise the registrable offender's compliance with a condition of the prohibition order to which the monitoring condition relates;

if the thing was seized under section 66Y(a)(ii), the police officer suspects on reasonable grounds that the thing relates to behaviour or conduct associated with an increased risk of the registrable offender contravening a condition to which the monitoring condition relates;
in any case, the thing is reasonably required for the purposes of an investigation of, or a proceeding for, an offence against this Act or any other Act; and
the thing is not subject to forfeiture, destruction or disposal under any other Act.

If the Chief Commissioner of Police is no longer authorised under section 66ZB(a) to retain a thing seized under section 66Y, the Chief Commissioner of Police must make reasonable efforts to notify in writing—
the registrable offender; or
if the Chief Commissioner believes that the registrable offender is not the owner of the thing, another person who the Chief Commissioner of Police believes to be the owner of the seized thing.
A notification under subsection (1) must be given in accordance with the regulations and include any prescribed information.

If the Chief Commissioner of Police has made reasonable efforts to notify a person in accordance with this section and the regulations, and the thing has not been retrieved, the thing is to be dealt with under Division 3 of Part 4 of the Victoria Police Act 2013 as if it were unclaimed property.

nodes.heading: Return of seized property—application to Magistrates' Court

nodes.text: The following persons may apply to the Magistrates' Court for the return of a thing seized under section 66Y—
the registrable offender;
if the registrable offender is not the owner of the thing seized, the owner.
The applicant must serve a copy of the application as soon as practicable on the Chief Commissioner of Police.
The Magistrates' Court may order the seized thing be returned to the applicant if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—
the Chief Commissioner of Police is not authorised to retain the thing under section 6ZB(a); and
the thing is not subject to forfeiture, destruction or disposal under this Act or any other Act.
The Magistrates' Court may refuse to make an order under subsection (3) if the Court is satisfied that the applicant is not the owner of the thing.

nodes.heading: Chief Commissioner of Police may apply for disposal order

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police may apply to the Magistrates' Court for an order that a thing seized under section 66Y may be destroyed or disposed of.
A copy of an application under subsection (1) must be served on the following persons as soon as practicable—
the registrable offender; and
if the Chief Commissioner believes that the registrable offender is not the owner of the thing, any other person who the Chief Commissioner of Police believes to be the owner of the seized thing.
On an application under this section, the Magistrates' Court may order—
that the seized thing be forfeited to the Crown and destroyed or disposed of in accordance with the order; or
that the thing be returned to the owner.
The Magistrates' Court may order that the seized thing be forfeited to the Crown and destroyed or disposed of in accordance with the order if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—
if the thing was seized under section 66Y(a), the Chief Commissioner of Police is authorised to retain the thing under section 66ZB(a)(i) or (ii); and
the thing is no longer reasonably required for the purposes of an investigation of or a proceeding for an offence against this Act or any other Act; and
the thing is not subject to forfeiture, destruction or disposal under any other Act.
If the Magistrates' Court orders that the seized thing be disposed of by sale, the Court may order that the proceeds of the sale be paid to the owner of the thing.
The Magistrates' Court may order that the seized thing be returned to the owner if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—
the Chief Commissioner of Police is not authorised to retain the thing under section 6ZB(a); and
the thing is not subject to forfeiture, destruction or disposal under any other Act.
An order under subsection (4) or (6) does not take effect until—
the day that is 30 days after the day on which the order was made; or
if an appeal is made before the expiry of the period referred to in paragraph (a), the appeal is determined.

nodes.heading: Destruction or disposal of seized things with owner's consent
nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police may destroy or dispose of a seized thing with the consent of the owner.

nodes.heading: Proceeds of sale or disposal to be paid into Consolidated Fund
nodes.text: Subject to an order to the contrary under section 66ZE(5), any amount received from the sale or disposal of seized things under this Division must be paid into the Consolidated Fund.

nodes.heading: Variation, extension and revocation of prohibition orders
Application to vary or revoke a prohibition order

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police or, subject to subsection (2), the registrable offender may apply to the court for an order varying or revoking a prohibition order.
The registrable offender may only apply for the variation or revocation of a prohibition order—
if the Chief Commissioner of Police consents to the making of the application; or
otherwise, with the leave of the court.
An application under subsection (1) must—
be made in writing; and
include the name of the registrable offender; and
include an affidavit setting out the grounds on which the variation or revocation of the prohibition order is sought; and
include any other information prescribed by the regulations.

The court may grant leave under subsection (2)(b) if satisfied that it is in the interests of justice to do so, having regard to changes in the registrable offender's circumstances, or circumstances affecting the registrable offender, since the prohibition order was made or last varied.

As soon as practicable after an application for an order varying or revoking a prohibition order is made, the application must be served on the registrable offender or the Chief Commissioner of Police (as the case requires).

nodes.heading: Application to extend a final prohibition order

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police may apply to the court for an order extending a final prohibition order.
An application under subsection (1) must—
be made in writing; and
include the name of the registrable offender; and
include an affidavit setting out the grounds on which extension of the final prohibition order is sought; and
include any other information prescribed by the regulations.
As soon as practicable after an application for an order extending a final prohibition order is made, the application must be served on the registrable offender.

nodes.heading: Considerations in determining whether to vary or revoke interim prohibition orders
nodes.text: In determining whether to vary or revoke an interim prohibition order, the court must have regard to—
the reasons for making the interim prohibition order; and
any change in the registrable offender's circumstances since the interim prohibition order was made or last varied.

nodes.heading: Considerations in varying, revoking or extending final prohibition orders

nodes.text: In determining whether to vary, revoke or extend a final prohibition order, the court must have regard to—
the reasons for making the final prohibition order; and
any change in the registrable offender's circumstances since the final prohibition order was made or last varied; and
the matters set out in section 66J; and
if the registrable offender is a child, the matters set out in section 66K; and
any other matters that the court considers relevant.
In determining an application for a variation, revocation or extension of a final prohibition order made against a registrable offender who is a child, the Children's Court may—
have regard to the assessment report, and any community treatment report, prepared for the hearing for the final prohibition order;
order the preparation of a new assessment report;
order the preparation of a community treatment report if—
the assessment report prepared for the hearing for the final prohibition order raised concerns about the impact on the child of making the final prohibition order; or
a new assessment report raises concerns about the impact on the child of varying or extending, or not revoking, the final prohibition order.
Section 66L applies in respect of a further assessment report ordered under subsection (2)(b), as if the report had been ordered by the Children's Court under section 66L(1).

nodes.heading: Court may vary a prohibition order

nodes.text: The court may vary an interim prohibition order if satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—

it is necessary to vary the order to reduce the risk that the registrable offender poses to the sexual safety of one or more persons or of children or the community generally pending a final decision about the application for a final prohibition order; or

one or more conditions of the order are no longer required to reduce the risk that the registrable offender poses to the sexual safety of one or more persons or of children or the community generally pending a final determination about the application for a final prohibition order; or
it is otherwise appropriate to vary the order, having regard to the registrable offender's specific needs.
The court may vary a final prohibition order if it is satisfied on the balance of probabilities that—
it is necessary to vary the order to reduce the risk that the registrable offender poses to the sexual safety of one or more persons, or of children or the community generally; or

one or more conditions of the order are no longer required to reduce the risk that the registrable offender poses to the sexual safety of one or more persons, or of children or the community generally; or
it is otherwise appropriate to vary the order, having regard to the registrable offender's specific needs.
If the registrable offender is an adult, the court may vary an interim prohibition order—
whether or not the registrable offender has been served with a copy of the application for the variation of the interim prohibition order; and
whether or not the registrable offender is present when the interim prohibition order is varied.
If the court varies a prohibition order, the court must give the registrable offender—
a copy of the prohibition order as varied by the order; and
a written notice that—
states that an order varying the prohibition order has been made; and
includes any other prescribed information.
The written notice and copy of the prohibition order as varied by the order must—
if the registrable offender is before the court, be given to the registrable offender with a copy of the order varying the prohibition order; or
if the registrable offender is not before the court, be served on the registrable offender with a copy of the order varying the prohibition order.

nodes.heading: Court may revoke a prohibition order

nodes.text: The court may revoke a prohibition order if it is satisfied on the balance of probabilities that the registrable offender does not pose a risk to the sexual safety of one or more persons, or of children or the community generally.

nodes.heading: Court may extend a final prohibition order

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), the court may extend the duration of a final prohibition order if satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that it is necessary to extend the duration of the order to reduce the risk that the registrable offender poses to the sexual safety of one or more persons, or of children or the community generally.
The court must not extend the duration of a final prohibition order to a date that—
if the registrable offender is an adult, is more than 5 years after the day on which the final prohibition order was made; or
if the registrable offender is a child, is more than 2 years after the day on which the final prohibition order was made; or
in any case, would be after the day on which the registrable offender's reporting period ends.
If the court makes an order extending the duration of a final prohibition order, the court must give the registrable offender—
a copy of the final prohibition order as extended by the order extending the final prohibition order; and
a written notice that—
states that an order extending the duration of the final prohibition order has been made; and
includes any other prescribed information.
The written notice and a copy of the final prohibition order as extended by the order extending the final prohibition order must—
if the registrable offender is before the court, be given to the registrable offender with the copy of the order extending the duration of the final prohibition order; or
if the registrable offender is not before the court, be served on the registrable offender with a copy of the order extending the duration of the final prohibition order.

nodes.heading: Court may make orders under this Division by consent

nodes.text: The court may make an order varying or revoking an interim prohibition order by consent of the parties—
without being satisfied as to any matter in section 66ZJ or—
section 66ZL(1), in the case of an order varying an interim prohibition order; or
section 66ZM(1), in the case of an order revoking an interim prohibition order; and
without conducting a hearing in relation to the particulars of the application unless, in the court's opinion, it is in the interests of justice to do so.
The court may make an order varying, revoking or extending a final prohibition order by consent of the parties—
without being satisfied as to any matter in section 66ZK or—
section 66ZL(2), in the case of an order varying a final prohibition order; or
section 66ZM(1), in the case of an order revoking a final prohibition order; or
section 66ZN(1), in the case of an order extending a final prohibition order; and
without conducting a hearing in relation to the particulars of the application unless, in the court's opinion, it is in the interests of justice to do so.
For the purposes of subsection (1)(b) and (2)(b), in determining whether it is in the interests of justice to conduct a hearing, the court may take into account whether the registrable offender—
is legally represented; or
is a child; or
has impaired intellectual functioning; or
is a person in respect of whom a guardianship order is in force; or
has the capacity to understand the proceeding; or
is subject to some other condition that may prevent the registrable offender from understanding the effect of consenting to the order.
This section applies to a registrable offender—
against whom a prohibition order has been made; and
who has been properly notified of the making of the order.
The registrable offender must not contravene the prohibition order without reasonable excuse.
Penalty: Level 6 imprisonment (5 years maximum).

nodes.heading: Application for registration of corresponding prohibition order

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police may apply for the registration of a corresponding prohibition order—
if the corresponding registrable offender is a child, to the Criminal Division of the Children's Court; or
in any other case, to the Magistrates' Court.
An application for a registration order must—
be made in writing; and
be accompanied by a copy of the corresponding prohibition order; and
include an affidavit stating that, at the time of making the application, the corresponding prohibition order is in force in the State or Territory in which it was made; and
if the Chief Commissioner of Police seeks to register the corresponding prohibition order with variations—
include details of the variations sought; and
include in the affidavit referred to in paragraph (c) the grounds on which those variations are sought.
An application for a registration order must be served on the corresponding registrable offender as soon as practicable after the application is made.

On application by the Chief Commissioner of Police under section 66ZQ, the court must make an order for the registration of a corresponding prohibition order if satisfied that, at the time the application was made, the corresponding prohibition order was in force in the State or Territory in which it was made.
Subject to section 66ZS, the court may vary the conditions of the corresponding prohibition order before making a registration order—
as sought in the application; or
as the court considers necessary to enable the enforcement of the order as a prohibition order.
The court may vary the conditions of a corresponding prohibition order under subsection (2) to include any condition the court could have included in a prohibition order under Division 5 or 6.
If the corresponding prohibition order is to be registered without variation, the court may make a registration order without conducting a hearing.

If the court makes a registration order without a hearing, as soon as practicable after the order is made, the court must cause the Chief Commissioner of Police to be notified of the registration order.

nodes.heading: Variation of corresponding prohibition order before registration if corresponding registrable offender is a child

nodes.text: If the corresponding registrable offender is a child, in determining whether to vary a corresponding prohibition order before registration, the Children's Court must have regard to the matters set out in section 66K.
The Children's Court may also—
order the preparation of an assessment report; and
if the assessment report raises concerns about the impact on the child of varying the corresponding prohibition order, request the preparation of a community treatment report.
Section 66L applies in respect of an assessment report ordered under subsection (2)(a), as if the report had been ordered by the Children's Court under section 66L(1).

nodes.heading: Corresponding registrable offender to be notified of registration order

nodes.text: If the court makes a registration order, the court must give the corresponding registrable offender a written notice that—
states that a registration order has been made; and
sets out the effect of the registration order, including—
that the corresponding prohibition order may be enforced against the corresponding registrable offender under this Act, as if it were a prohibition order; and
that it is an offence to contravene a prohibition order, and the maximum penalties that apply to a contravention; and
that the registration order ceases to have effect if the corresponding prohibition order ceases to have effect in the State or Territory in which it was made; and
includes any other prescribed information.
A written notice under subsection (1) must—
if the corresponding registrable offender is before the court, be given to the corresponding registrable offender with a copy of the registration order; or
if the registrable offender is not before the court, be served on the corresponding registrable offender with a copy of the registration order.

nodes.heading: Duration of registration order
nodes.text: Unless it is earlier revoked, a registration order expires on—
the day on which the corresponding prohibition order (as in force at the time of registration) expires; or
if the court specifies an earlier day, that day.
The expiry of a registration order has no effect on the validity of the corresponding prohibition order.

Subject to subsection (2), if a corresponding registrable offender has been properly notified of the making of a registration order, the corresponding prohibition order (whether varied before registration or not) may be enforced against the corresponding registrable offender as if it were a prohibition order.

A registration order cannot be enforced against the corresponding registrable offender if the corresponding prohibition order has expired or otherwise has ceased to have effect in the State or Territory in which it was made.
A registration order may be revoked under section 66ZZA if the corresponding prohibition order has ceased to have effect in the State or Territory in which it was made.

nodes.heading: No effect in Victoria if corresponding prohibition order varied or extended by interstate court
nodes.text: The variation or extension of a corresponding prohibition order by a court of the State or Territory in which it was made after the order is registered under this Division has no effect in Victoria.

nodes.heading: Application for variation of a registration order

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police or, subject to subsection (2), the corresponding registrable offender may apply to the court for an order varying a registration order.
The corresponding registrable offender may only apply for an order varying a registration order—
if the Chief Commissioner of Police consents to the making of the application; or
in any other case, with the leave of the court.

The court may grant leave under subsection (2)(b) if satisfied that it is in the interests of justice, having regard to changes in the corresponding registrable offender's circumstances, or circumstances affecting the corresponding registrable offender, since the registration order was made or last varied.

As soon as practicable after an application under subsection (1) is made, the application must be served on the corresponding registrable offender or the Chief Commissioner of Police (as the case requires).

nodes.heading: Considerations in making an order varying a registration order

nodes.text: In determining whether to vary a registration order, the court must have regard to—
the reasons for making the registration order; and
any change in the corresponding registrable offender's circumstances since the registration order was made or last varied; and
the matters set out in section 66J and, if the corresponding registrable offender is a child, section 66K; and
any other matters that the court considers relevant.
In determining an application for variation of a registration order made against a corresponding registrable offender who is a child, the Children's Court may—
have regard to any assessment report and community treatment report prepared for the hearing for the registration order;
order the preparation of a new assessment report;
if an assessment report referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) raises concerns about the impact of varying the registration order on the child, order the preparation of a community treatment report.
Section 66L applies in respect of an assessment report ordered under subsection (2)(b), as if the report had been ordered by the Children's Court under section 66L(1).

nodes.heading: Court may vary a registration order

nodes.text: The court may vary a registration order—
if satisfied that—

there has been a change in the corresponding registrable offender's circumstances since the registration order was made so that a variation is necessary to enable enforcement of the registration order; or
the corresponding prohibition order has been varied in the State or Territory in which it was made, and a corresponding variation of the registration order is appropriate; or
in the case of an application for variation made by the corresponding registrable offender, if the Chief Commissioner of Police consents to the variation.
The court may vary a registration order to include any condition the court could have included in a prohibition order under Division 5 or 6.
If the court varies a registration order, the court must give the corresponding registrable offender a written notice that—
states that an order varying the registration order has been made; and
includes any other prescribed information.
The written notice must—
if the corresponding registrable offender is before the court, be given to the corresponding registrable offender with a copy of the order varying the registration order; or
if the corresponding registrable offender is not before the court, be served on the corresponding registrable offender with a copy of the order varying the registration order.

On a written application made by the Chief Commissioner of Police, the court must revoke a registration order if it is satisfied that the corresponding prohibition order is no longer in effect in the State or Territory in which it was made.

nodes.heading: Court may prohibit publication of proceedings

nodes.text: The court may order that a person must not publish, or cause to be published, a report of a proceeding under this Part or about an order made under this Part that contains any particulars likely to lead to the identification of—
the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender; or
a victim of an offence committed by the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender; or
any person protected by a prohibition order, a registration order or a corresponding prohibition order.
For the purposes of subsection (1), the particulars likely to lead to the identification of a person include, but are not limited to, the following—
the person's name, title, pseudonym or alias;
the address of any premises at which the person lives or works, or the locality in which the premises are situated;
the address of a school attended by the person or the locality in which the school is situated;
the physical description or the style of dress of the person;
any employment or occupation engaged in, profession practised or calling pursued by, the person or any official or honorary position held by the person;

the relationship of the person to identified relatives of the person or the association of the person with identified friends or identified business, official or professional acquaintances of the person;
the recreational interests or the political, philosophical or religious beliefs or interests of the person;
any real or personal property in which the person has an interest or with which the person is associated.
An order under subsection (1) does not prohibit the publication of particulars that are likely to lead to the identification of a registrable offender by—
the Chief Commissioner of Police under section 61A(1); or
if those particulars have been published by the Chief Commissioner of Police under section 61A(1), any other person.

nodes.heading: Chief Commissioner of Police may disclose personal information about prohibition orders and registration orders

nodes.text: If the Chief Commissioner of Police believes on reasonable grounds that the disclosure is necessary for the purposes of an order made under this Part (other than an order made under section 66ZD or 66ZE), the Chief Commissioner may disclose personal information relating to the order or the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender against whom the order was made—
if the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender is a child, to a parent of the child; or
to a parent of a named child protected by the order; or
subject to subsection (2), to any other person.
The Chief Commissioner of Police may only disclose information under subsection (1)(c) if the disclosure is reasonably necessary for the enforcement of the order.
If the Chief Commissioner of Police discloses information to a person under this section, the disclosure must—
be made in writing; and
state that it is an offence for the person to disclose personal information to another person.
A person to whom personal information has been disclosed in accordance with this section must not disclose that information to any person.
Penalty: 60 penalty units or imprisonment for 6 months or both.

nodes.heading: Service of orders and applications made by Chief Commissioner of Police

nodes.text: An application made by the Chief Commissioner of Police under this Part (other than an application under section 66ZF) must be served personally on the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender by a police officer.

If the court makes a prohibition order or a registration order, or an order varying, revoking or extending a prohibition order or registration order, a copy of the order must be served personally on the registrable offender or corresponding registrable offender by a police officer.
The court may not make an order for substituted service in respect of an application or order referred to in this section.

nodes.heading: Registrable offenders prohibited from child-related employment

nodes.text: In this Part—

history.raw: S. 67(1) def. of contact repealed by No. 82/2014 s. 23.
S. 67(1) def. of registered sex offender repealed by No. 25/2017 s. 43(b).

nodes.heading: child-related employment
nodes.text: means employment involving contact with a child in connection with—

history.raw: S. 67(1) def. of child-related employment amended by Nos 57/2005 s. 51(1), 48/2006 s. 42(Sch. item 33.6), 80/2011 s. 79(Sch. item 6).

nodes.text: child protection services;
child care services mentioned in section 194(1) of the A New Tax System (Family Assistance) (Administration) Act 1999 of the Commonwealth;
children's services within the meaning of the Children's Services Act 1996;
education and care services within the meaning of the Education and Care Services National Law (Victoria);
educational institutions;

community services, remand centres, youth residential centres, youth supervision units or youth justice centres, within the meaning of the Children, Youth and Families Act 2005 or probation services under that Act;
refuges or other residential facilities used by children;
paediatric wards of public hospitals within the meaning of the Health Services Act 1988 or of private hospitals within the meaning of that Act;

clubs, associations or movements (including of a cultural, recreational or sporting nature) that provide services or conduct activities for, or directed at, children or whose membership is mainly comprised of children;
religious organisations;
baby sitting or child minding services arranged by a commercial agency;
fostering children;
providing, on a publicly-funded or commercial basis, a transport service specifically for children;
coaching or private tuition services of any kind for children;
counselling or other support services for children;
overnight camps for children regardless of the type of accommodation or of how many children are involved;
school crossing services, being services provided by people employed to assist children to cross roads on their way to or from school;
providing, on a commercial basis and not merely incidentally to or in support of other business activities, an entertainment or party service specifically for children;
providing, on a commercial basis and not merely incidentally to or in support of other business activities, gym or play facilities specifically for children;
The provision of play facilities for children by a fast-food business may be merely incidental to the business of providing food.
providing, on a commercial basis and not merely incidentally to or in support of other business activities, photography services specifically for children;
talent or beauty competitions held for children on a commercial basis and not merely incidentally to or in support of other business activities;

nodes.heading: educational institution
nodes.text: means—

history.raw: S. 67(1) def. of educational institutions for children substituted as educational institution by No. 57/2005 s. 51(2), substituted by No. 24/2006 s. 6.1.2(Sch. 7 item 36.1(a)), amended by Nos 76/2013 s. 22, 32/2022 s. 65.

nodes.text: any Government school or non-Government school within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006; or
any of the following—
a TAFE institute within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006;
a dual sector university within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006;
a provider of adult, community and further education, within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006, that is eligible for funding under that Act;
an education and training organisation registered on the State Register under the Education and Training Reform Act 2006—

to the extent that the college, university, provider, institution or organisation provides a program of study or training primarily for, or directed at, children, and that leads to the award of a Senior Secondary Certificate of Education that is recognised by the AQF within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006; or
any other institution that provides a program of study or training primarily for, or directed at, children—
but does not include—
except to the extent provided by paragraph (b), a university within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006; or
except to the extent provided by paragraph (b), a TAFE institute within the meaning of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006—
even if that university, college or institution has a student under 18 years of age;

nodes.heading: employment
nodes.text: means—
performance of work—
under a contract of employment or a contract for services (whether written or unwritten); or
for gain or reward other than under a contract of employment or contract for services; or
as a minister of religion or as part of the duties of a religious vocation; or

undertaking practical training as part of an educational or vocational course other than under an arrangement under Part 5.4 of the Education and Training Reform Act 2006 if the student is of or under 18 years of age; or
performance of work as a volunteer including the performance of unpaid community work under—
a drug and alcohol treatment order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991; or
an old community-based order within the meaning of clause 1 of Schedule 3 to the Sentencing Act 1991; or
an old intensive correction order within the meaning of clause 1 of Schedule 3 to the Sentencing Act 1991; or
a fine conversion order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991; or
a fine default unpaid community work order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991; or
performance of work as a volunteer including the performance of unpaid community work under a community correction order within the meaning of the Sentencing Act 1991;

history.raw: S. 67(1) def. of officer amended by No. 25/2017 s. 43(a).

nodes.text: in relation to a body corporate that is a corporation within the meaning of the Corporations Act, has the same meaning as in section 9 of that Act; and
in relation to any other body corporate, means any person (by whatever name called) who is concerned or takes part in the management of the body corporate.
For the purposes of this Act, a person is engaged in child-related employment if he or she is—
an officer of a body corporate that is engaged in child-related employment; or
a member of the committee of management of an unincorporated body or association that is engaged in child-related employment; or
a member of a partnership that is engaged in child-related employment.

nodes.heading: Registrable offender excluded from child-related employment

nodes.text: A registrable offender must not—
apply for; or
engage in—
employment that is child-related employment.
Penalty: 240 penalty units or imprisonment for 2 years.
In a proceeding for an offence against subsection
, it is a defence to the charge for the accused to prove that, at the time the offence is alleged to have been committed, he or she did not know that the employment was child-related employment.

nodes.heading: Offence to fail to disclose charges

nodes.text: A person engaged in child-related employment (including employment under a contract for services) who is charged with a registrable offence must disclose the charge to his or her employer within 7 days after the filing of the charge-sheet charging the offence or (in the case of a charge that is pending immediately before the commencement of this subsection) within 7 days after that commencement.

history.raw: S. 69(1) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 112.5).

nodes.text: Penalty: 60 penalty units.

A person who applies for employment (including employment under a contract for services) that is child-related employment and against whom there is a pending charge of a registrable offence must disclose the charge to his or her prospective employer at the time of making the application.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.

A person who has (whether before or after the commencement of this subsection) applied for employment (including employment under a contract for services) that is child-related employment and who, while the application is still current, is charged with a registrable offence must disclose the charge to his or her prospective employer within 7 days after the filing of the charge-sheet charging the offence or (in the case of a charge that is pending immediately before the commencement of this subsection) within 7 days after that commencement.

history.raw: S. 69(3) amended by No. 68/2009 s. 97(Sch. item 112.5).

nodes.text: Penalty: 60 penalty units.
A person must not give to any other person, whether directly or indirectly, any information acquired by the person under section 69.
Penalty: 60 penalty units.
Subsection (1) does not apply to the giving of information—
to a court or tribunal in the course of legal proceedings; or
pursuant to an order of a court or tribunal; or
to the extent reasonably required to enable the investigation or the enforcement of a law of this State or of any other State or of a Territory or of the Commonwealth; or
to an Australian legal practitioner for the purpose of obtaining legal advice or representation relating to a matter under this Act; or

history.raw: S. 70(2)(d) amended by Nos 18/2005 s. 18(Sch. 1 item 99), 17/2014 s. 160(Sch. 2 item 90).

nodes.text: with the written authority of the person to whom the information relates or, if the person to whom the information relates is a child or a person with a cognitive impairment or mental illness within the meaning of Subdivision (8E) of Division 1 of Part I of the Crimes Act 1958, with the written authority of a person authorised to act on that person's behalf; or
in good faith for the purposes of this Act; or
as required or authorised by or under any other Act.

history.raw: Pt 5A (Heading and ss 70A–70K) inserted by No. 52/2007 s. 20.

nodes.heading: Application of Part
nodes.text: This Part applies despite anything to the contrary in the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996.

nodes.heading: Definitions
nodes.text: In this Part—

history.raw: S. 70B def. of Victorian Registrar repealed by No. 25/2019 s. 36(b).

nodes.heading: change of name application
nodes.text: means an application by or on behalf of a registrable offender for registration of a change of the offender's name for which approval is required under section 70C;

nodes.heading: Interstate Registrar
nodes.text: means an authority responsible under a law of another State or Territory for the registration of births, deaths and marriages.

history.raw: S. 70B def. of Interstate Registrar amended by No. 25/2019 s. 36(a).

nodes.heading: Applications for change of name by or on behalf of a registrable offender

nodes.text: A registrable offender must not—
apply to the Victorian Registrar to register a change of his or her name under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996; or
apply to an Interstate Registrar to register a change of his or her name under a law of another State or Territory that is the equivalent of the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996—
without having first obtained the written approval of the Chief Commissioner of Police.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
A person must not, on behalf of a registrable offender—
apply to the Victorian Registrar to register a change of his or her name under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996; or
apply to an Interstate Registrar to register a change of his or her name under a law of another State or Territory that is the equivalent of the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996—
without having first obtained the written approval of the Chief Commissioner of Police.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.

nodes.heading: Approval by Chief Commissioner of Police

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), the Chief Commissioner of Police may only approve a change of name application if the Chief Commissioner is satisfied that the change of name is in all the circumstances necessary or reasonable.
The Chief Commissioner of Police must not approve a change of name application if the Chief Commissioner is satisfied that the change of name would, if registered, be reasonably likely—
to be regarded as offensive by a victim of crime or an appreciable sector of the community; or
to frustrate the administration of this Act in respect of the registrable offender.

nodes.heading: Approval to be notified in writing
nodes.text: If the Chief Commissioner of Police approves a change of name application, the Chief Commissioner must—
as soon as practicable, give written notice of the approval to the person who made the application; and
if the registrable offender consents, give a copy of the written notice of approval to the Victorian Registrar or the Interstate Registrar (as the case so requires).
The Victorian Registrar must not register a change of name under the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996 if—
the Victorian Registrar knows that—
the application for the change of name is made by or on behalf of a registrable offender; and
the change of name relates to the name of the registrable offender; and
the Victorian Registrar has not received a copy of the notice of approval of the Chief Commissioner of Police under section 70E.

If the Victorian Registrar does not register a change of name because of the operation of subsection (1), the Victorian Registrar must give written notice of the application to the Chief Commissioner of Police.

nodes.heading: Registrar may correct Register
nodes.text: Without limiting section 43 of the Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1996, the Victorian Registrar may correct the Register under that section if—
the name of a registrable offender on the Register has been changed; and
the Chief Commissioner of Police has not approved that change under this Part.

nodes.heading: Lapse of application where offender ceases to be a registrable offender
nodes.text: A change of name application under this Part by or on behalf of an offender lapses if—
the registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender; and
the Victorian Registrar has not registered the change of name before the registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender.

nodes.heading: Information-sharing between the Secretary and the Victorian Registrar

nodes.text: Despite any law to the contrary—

the Secretary or the Chief Commissioner of Police may notify the Victorian Registrar of the name (including any other name by which a registrable offender is or has previously been known), date of birth and residential address or addresses of the registrable offender; and

if the Secretary or the Chief Commissioner of Police has given notification under paragraph (a) in respect of a registrable offender, the Secretary or the Chief Commissioner must notify the Victorian Registrar as soon as practicable after the registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender.
Nothing in this section affects the operation of the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities.

nodes.heading: Registrable offender who is also subject to a supervision or detention order

history.raw: S. 70J inserted by No. 52/2007 s. 20, substituted by No. 91/2009 s. 219(Sch. 3 item 3).

nodes.text: This section applies to a registrable offender who is also subject to a supervision order, an interim supervision order, a detention order, an interim detention order or an emergency detention order within the meaning of the Serious Offenders Act 2018.

history.raw: S. 70J(1) amended by No. 43/2012 s. 3(Sch. item 48), substituted by Nos 25/2017 s. 45(2), 27/2018 s. 365(4).

nodes.text: Despite this Part, an application by or on behalf of a registrable offender to whom this section applies for registration of a change of the offender's name must be made under and in accordance with the Serious Offenders Act 2018.

nodes.heading: Registrable offender who is also a prisoner on parole
nodes.text: Despite this Part, an application by or on behalf of a registrable offender who is also a prisoner on parole within the meaning of Division 6 of Part 8 of the Corrections Act 1986 for registration of a change of the offender's name must be made under and in accordance with that Division of that Part of that Act.

history.raw: Pt 5B (Heading and ss 70L–70P) inserted by No. 21/2016 s. 15.

nodes.heading: IBAC to monitor compliance with Parts 3 and 4

nodes.text: The IBAC is to monitor compliance with Part 3 by the Chief Commissioner of Police and persons authorised to receive reports.

The IBAC is to monitor compliance with Part 4 by the Chief Commissioner of Police and other persons authorised by the Chief Commissioner of Police to have access to the Register of Sex Offenders or any part of that Register.

nodes.heading: IBAC to be given reasonable assistance
nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police must ensure that each of the following persons gives the IBAC any assistance that the IBAC reasonably requires to enable the IBAC to perform the IBAC's functions under this Part—
police officers and other persons authorised by the Chief Commissioner of Police to have access to the Register of Sex Offenders;
persons authorised to receive reports under Part 3.
An authorised officer may, after notifying the Chief Commissioner of Police of the intended entry—

enter at any time premises occupied by Victoria Police at which the IBAC Commissioner reasonably believes there are documents that contain, or relate to, the Register of Sex Offenders or any part of that Register or that are relevant to the IBAC's functions under this Part; and
inspect or copy any document found at any premises entered under paragraph (a); and
do anything that it is necessary or convenient to do to enable an inspection to be carried out under this section.
For the purposes of this section, an authorised officer is—
the IBAC Commissioner; or
a sworn IBAC Officer who is authorised under subsection (3).
The IBAC may authorise a sworn IBAC Officer to exercise the powers of an authorised officer under this section.
The IBAC may at any time give the Minister a written report on—
the results of any inspections carried out under section 70N; and
compliance with Part 3 in the period to which the report relates by the Chief Commissioner of Police and police officers receiving reports; and

compliance with Part 4 in the period to which the report relates by the Chief Commissioner of Police and other persons authorised by the Chief Commissioner of Police to have access to the Register of Sex Offenders or any part of that Register.
If requested by the Minister to do so, the IBAC must give the Minister a report under subsection
as soon as practicable after receiving the request.
The IBAC must give a copy of any report under subsection (1) to the Chief Commissioner of Police.

The Chief Commissioner of Police must advise the Minister of any information included in a copy of a report received under subsection (3) that, in the Chief Commissioner's opinion, should be excluded from the report before the report is laid before Parliament because the information could be reasonably expected to—
endanger a person's safety; or
prejudice an investigation or prosecution; or
compromise operational activities or methodologies of Victoria Police or the IBAC.
The Minister must—
exclude information from the report if satisfied on the advice of the Chief Commissioner of Police of any of the grounds set out in subsection (4); and
cause a copy of a report under this section to be laid before each House of Parliament within 15 sitting days after the day on which the Minister receives the report.

nodes.heading: Chief Commissioner of Police to report to Minister

nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police must report to the Minister, before 30 September in each year, on the following matters—
the total number of registrable offenders as at the immediately preceding 30 June;
the number of offenders added to the Register in the financial year ending on the immediately preceding 30 June;
the number of prohibition orders made in the financial year ending on the immediately preceding 30 June;
the number of registration orders made in the financial year ending on the immediately preceding 30 June;
any other prescribed information.

The Minister must cause the information reported under subsection (1) to be included in Victoria Police's annual report of operations for a financial year under Part 7 of the Financial Management Act 1994.
The Chief Commissioner of Police must not report under subsection (1) any personal information unless the information is de-identified information.
For the purposes of subsection (3), de-identified information has the same meaning as in section 64A.

nodes.heading: Approval of making of acknowledgement of sex applications— registrable offenders

history.raw: Pt 5C (Headings and ss 70Q– 70W) inserted by No. 25/2019 s. 37.

nodes.heading: Offence to make acknowledgement of sex application without approval

nodes.text: A registrable offender must not make an acknowledgement of sex application to a Registrar without having first obtained the written approval of the Chief Commissioner of Police.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.
A person must not make an acknowledgement of sex application to a Registrar on behalf of a registrable offender unless the written approval of the Chief Commissioner of Police is first obtained.
Penalty: 5 penalty units.

nodes.heading: Application by registrable offender or other person for approval of Chief Commissioner of Police
nodes.text: A registrable offender or other person who intends to make an acknowledgement of sex application may apply to the Chief Commissioner of Police for approval of the making of the acknowledgement of sex application by the registrable offender or the person.

nodes.heading: Approval by Chief Commissioner of Police of the making of acknowledgement of sex application

nodes.text: Subject to subsection (2), on an application under section 70R, the Chief Commissioner of Police may approve the making of an acknowledgement of sex application if the Chief Commissioner of Police is satisfied that the alteration of the record of sex or the issuing of a document acknowledging name and sex is, in all the circumstances, necessary or reasonable.

The Chief Commissioner of Police must not approve the making of an acknowledgement of sex application if the Chief Commissioner of Police is satisfied that the alteration of the record of sex or the issuing of a document acknowledging name and sex would be reasonably likely—
to be regarded as offensive by a victim of crime or an appreciable sector of the community; or
to frustrate the administration of this Act in respect of the registrable offender.

nodes.heading: Copy of approval or refusal of Chief Commissioner of Police

nodes.text: If the Chief Commissioner of Police approves the making of an acknowledgement of sex application, the Chief Commissioner of Police as soon as practicable must give a copy of the approval to—
the person who sought the approval; and
the Victorian Registrar.
If the Chief Commissioner of Police refuses to approve the making of an acknowledgement of sex application the Chief Commissioner of Police must give a copy of that refusal to—
the person who sought the approval; and
the Secretary.
See section 70I for information shared between the Secretary or the Chief Commissioner of Police and the Victorian Registrar.

nodes.heading: Lapse of application where registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender
nodes.text: An acknowledgement of sex application by or on behalf of a registrable offender lapses if—
the registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender; and
the Victorian Registrar has not registered the alteration of the record of sex or issued the document acknowledging name and sex before the registrable offender ceases to be a registrable offender.

nodes.heading: Registrable offender who is also subject to a supervision or detention order

nodes.text: This section applies to a registrable offender who is also subject to a supervision order, an interim supervision order, a detention order, an interim detention order or an emergency detention order within the meaning of the Serious Offenders Act 2018.

Despite this Part, an application by or on behalf of a registrable offender to whom this section applies for the appropriate approval to make an acknowledgement of sex application must be made under and in accordance with Part 17A of the Serious Offenders Act 2018.

nodes.heading: Registrable offender who is also a prisoner on parole
nodes.text: Despite this Part, an application for the appropriate approval to make an acknowledgement of sex application by or on behalf of a registrable offender who is also a prisoner on parole within the meaning of Division 6A of Part 8 of the Corrections Act 1986 must be made in accordance with Division 6A of Part 8 of the Corrections Act 1986.

nodes.heading: Authorised disclosures of information to affected persons

history.raw: Pt 5D (Heading and ss 70X–70ZH) inserted by No. 55/2025 s. 73.

nodes.heading: Definitions for this Part
nodes.text: In this Part—

nodes.heading: affected person
nodes.text: means any of the following—
a victim of a registrable offence committed by a registrable offender;
a parent of a person referred to in paragraph (a) who—
is a child; or
was a child at the time the offence occurred;

nodes.heading: affected person's representative
nodes.text: means—
a person nominated under section 70ZB by an affected person; or
in the case of an affected person included in the victims register, a nominee included in the victims register for that person;

nodes.heading: authorised person
nodes.text: means any of the following—
an affected person;
a person included in the victims register or previously included in the victims register in relation to the registrable offender;
a family member of the affected person, including a parent of the affected person;
a member of Victoria Police personnel performing a function, exercising a power or discharging a duty under this Act;

a police officer, the Director of Public Prosecutions or a person employed in the Office of Public Prosecutions established under the Public Prosecutions Act 1994 if that police officer or person is investigating an offence;
a registered medical practitioner in the course of treatment of an affected person or affected person's representative;
a person registered as a psychologist under the Health Practitioner Regulation National Law in the course of treatment of an affected person or affected person's representative;
a lawyer in the course of consulting that lawyer for legal advice;

nodes.heading: Director of Public Prosecutions
nodes.text: means the Director of Public Prosecutions appointed under section 87AB of the Constitution Act 1975;

nodes.heading: relevant application
nodes.text: means any of the following—
an application for a sex offender registration order;
an application for a registration exemption order;
an application under section 39 or 39A for a suspension order;
an application under section 44A to revoke a suspension order;
an application under Part 5A for approval of a change of name application;
an application under section 70R for approval of an acknowledgement of sex application that includes a change of name;

nodes.heading: relevant event
nodes.text: means any of the following—
the making of a sex offender registration order under section 11(1), (2) or (9);
a suspension order ceasing to have effect by operation of section 44(1) or 44A(2);
the reviving of a suspension order under section 44(2);

nodes.heading: relevant matter
nodes.text: means any of the following—
a suspension of reporting obligations under section 45A;
a cancellation of suspension of reporting obligations under section 45A;

nodes.heading: suspension order
nodes.text: means an order made by a court under section 40 suspending a registrable offender's reporting obligations;

nodes.heading: victims register
nodes.text: has the same meaning as it has in the Corrections Act 1986.

nodes.heading: Chief Commissioner of Police may disclose certain information to affected persons

nodes.text: Subject to this section and section 70Z, the Chief Commissioner of Police may disclose any information specified in section 70ZA to an affected person if any of the following applies—
the disclosure is made for the purposes of performing functions or exercising powers in relation to any relevant application or relevant matter;
a relevant application has been made;
a relevant event has occurred.
If an affected person has nominated a representative, the Chief Commissioner of Police may disclose information under subsection (1) to the representative on behalf of the affected person.

If the affected person is a child, the Chief Commissioner of Police may disclose information under subsection (1) to a parent of the child or a representative nominated by a parent instead of the child or a representative nominated by the child after having regard to—
the child's capacity to receive the disclosure or nominate a representative; and
any preferences for contact expressed by the child and the child's capacity to express those preferences.
This section does not apply if—
the disclosure relates to a registrable offender who is a person to whom Division 9 of Part 3 applies; or
the disclosure of the information would be contrary to an order made by a court.
In deciding whether to disclose specified information under section 70Y the Chief Commissioner of Police must have regard to the following—
the welfare of the affected person;
the affected person's preferences (if any) as to contact;
any other matter the Chief Commissioner of Police considers relevant.
The Chief Commissioner of Police may also have regard to—
the welfare of any other affected person; and
the capacity of the affected person to receive a disclosure, nominate a representative or express a preference as to contact; and

if the disclosure under section 70Y(1) is made to a parent or representative of a parent instead of a child, the parent's welfare and capacity to receive a disclosure, nominate a representative or express a preference as to contact.
For the purposes of section 70Y(1), the following information is specified about a relevant application or relevant matter—
the name of the registrable offender;
the nature of the relevant application or relevant matter;
in the case of a relevant application made to a court, details about how to find information about the date, time and place of the hearing;
the decision of the court or the Chief Commissioner of Police (as the case requires) in relation to the relevant application or relevant matter, including—
if the relevant application is an application for a sex offender registration order, the reporting period specified in the order; and
if the relevant application or relevant matter relates to a suspension of reporting obligations, the period for which the registrable offender's reporting obligations are suspended; and
if the relevant application is an application for approval of change of name or approval of an acknowledgement of sex, the name registered and date on which it was registered by the Registrar;
the date on which the decision was made by the court or the Chief Commissioner of Police.
For the purposes of section 70Y(1), the following information is specified in relation to a relevant event—
the name of the registrable offender;
in the case of the making of a sex offender registration order under section 11(1), (2) or
the date on which the order was made; and
the reporting period specified in the order;
in the case of a suspension order that has ceased to have effect—
the order that has ceased to have effect; and
the date on which it ceased to have effect; and
the reason that the order ceased to have effect;
if the suspension order has been revived by operation of section 44(2)—
the order that has been revived; and
the date on which it was revived; and
the reason that the order has been revived.

nodes.heading: Affected person may nominate contact preferences and representative

nodes.text: An affected person may notify the Chief Commissioner of Police from time to time of the affected person's preference as to contact for the purposes of receiving a disclosure of information under section 70Y.
An affected person may nominate a representative to receive a disclosure under section 70Y on their behalf.
A nomination under subsection (2) must be made in the form approved by the Chief Commissioner of Police and include the name and contact details of the person nominated as a representative.

nodes.heading: Secretary may give Chief Commissioner of Police information included in victims register
nodes.text: If requested by the Chief Commissioner of Police for the purposes of disclosing information under this Part, the Secretary may—
advise the Chief Commissioner of Police—
whether an affected person is included in the victims register in respect of a registrable offence committed by the registrable offender; and
if that affected person is included in the victims register, the name of any nominee; and

give to the Chief Commissioner of Police the contact details and contact preferences of an affected person included in the victims register and of any nominee included for that affected person in the victims register.

nodes.heading: Record of contact preferences and details
nodes.text: The Chief Commissioner of Police must keep a record of—
contact details and contact preferences of an affected person notified under section 70ZB or obtained under section 70ZC; and
the name, contact details and contact preferences of any affected person's representative notified under section 70ZB or obtained under section 70ZC.

nodes.heading: Obligation to maintain confidentiality of information disclosed—affected person or affected person's representative

nodes.text: An affected person or an affected person's representative to whom information is disclosed under section 70Y must maintain the confidential nature of the information.
An affected person or affected person's representative does not fail to maintain the confidential nature of the information merely by—

in the case of an affected person's representative or a parent of an affected person, disclosing the information to the affected person on whose behalf the disclosure under section 70Y was received; or
in any case, disclosing the information to an authorised person.
A disclosure in circumstances referred to in subsection (2) does not affect the confidential nature of the information.
For the purposes of this section, information disclosed under section 70Y is no longer confidential in nature if it lawfully enters the public domain.

nodes.heading: Obligation to maintain confidentiality—authorised persons and third parties

nodes.text: This section applies to a person who—
receives information that was disclosed to an affected person or an affected person's representative under section 70Y; and
knows or ought reasonably to have known that the information was disclosed to an affected person or an affected person's representative under section 70Y by the Chief Commissioner of Police.
The person must maintain the confidential nature of that information.
For the purposes of this section, information disclosed under section 70Y is no longer confidential in nature if it lawfully enters the public domain.

nodes.heading: Offence to publish information disclosed under this Part

nodes.text: A person must not publish any information about a registrable offender if—
the information was disclosed to an affected person or an affected person's representative under section 70Y; and
the person knows or ought reasonably to have known that the information was disclosed to an affected person or an affected person's representative under section 70Y.
